evidence_text: Table 1 indicated that corrosion potential and current density decreased with an increase in BALE concentrations up to 3000ppm and then slightly increased. Based on those results, inhibition efficiency was calculated using the following formula: $$ η\left(%\right) = \left(1 - \frac{i_{corr}}{i_{corr}^{0}}\right)\times 100% \tag{(1)} $$ where η: inhibition efficiency (%), i$_{corr}$: corrosion current density of the inhibited system, and i$^{0}$ $_{corr}$: corrosion current density of the uninhibited system. Fig. 3(b) presents the inhibition efficiency that indicated a high inhibition efficiency of the BALE and the inhibition efficiency was increased with increasing of BALE concentrations up to 3000ppm and then its slight decrease at higher concentration. In addition, the comparison of corrosion inhibition performance between B. acutangula and some reported leaf extracts is shown in Table 2, in which all leaf extracts performed as a mixed cathodic-anodic inhibitor.
